title: standings computes factually wrong tables: clubs collapse by name, no season default
evidence: src/brazilian_soccer_mcp/core.clj:30 normalize-name strips the state suffix via regex \s*-\s*[a-z]{2}$, so Atletico-MG, Atletico-PR and Atletico-GO all become "atletico". standings (core.clj:118-121) builds rows from distinct :home-team/:away-team strings but team-statistics re-filters by normalized key, so each Atletico row is credited with ALL three clubs' matches. _factual.json confirms: Atletico-GO/MG/PR rows are byte-identical (played=926, points=1371, win-rate=40.71) and the 2019 table shows 19 of 20 clubs (Atletico merged). standings also has no default season (core.clj:118 (defn standings [season])): with season nil, find-matches applies no season filter and returns all-time totals (Flamengo played=410, not 38). factual_accuracy=0.0 in scores.json.
suggestion: Key standings on the full club name (including -XX suffix) rather than the suffix-stripped normalize-name, and give standings a sensible default (latest season) or require season explicitly.

title: normalize-name suffix-stripping silently merges distinct clubs across all tools
evidence: src/brazilian_soccer_mcp/core.clj:30 (str/replace #"\s*-\s*[a-z]{2}$" ""). The same collapse affects find-matches (:team Atletico-MG matches PR+GO games too), team-statistics and head-to-head, not just standings. Correct for teams with a unique base name but wrong for the three Atletico/Athletico clubs that coexisted in Serie A.
suggestion: Normalize only accents/whitespace/case; keep the -XX state suffix (or map to canonical club ids) so state-distinguished clubs stay separate.

title: tests use a 2-row inline fixture, never the real CSVs, so the standings defect is uncaught
evidence: test/brazilian_soccer_mcp/core_test.clj:4 defines a 2-match fixture with pre-set distinct :home-key/:away-key; no test calls load-data or standings against data/kaggle/, so the normalize-name collision and no-season-default bugs pass all 3 deftests (test_coverage=1.0).
suggestion: Add a test that loads the real data and asserts (standings 2019) yields 20 clubs each with played=38.
